display.description:
Request and response bytes per second measured by Traefik. Compare with traffic to spot unusually large payloads.

Measurement details:
Request and response payload bytes for selected services. This is not total network-interface traffic.
display.name: Data transferred per second (bytes/s)

display.description:
Requests per second grouped by response code. Use this to distinguish successful responses, redirects, rejected requests and server errors.

Measurement details:
2xx means success; 3xx redirection; 4xx client error or rejection; 5xx server failure. Code zero is a proxy or connection outcome.
display.name: Traffic by HTTP response code

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_replace((label_join((sum by (code) ((sum by (cluster_name,service,protocol,code,method) ((max by (cluster_name,instance,service,protocol,code,method,le) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}",protocol="http"}[5m]))) or ((label_replace(rate(_traefik_service_requests{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}",protocol="http",traefik_backend!=""}[5m]), "service", "$1", "traefik_backend", "(.*)")) unless on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name,instance,service,protocol,code,method,le) (rate(traefik_service_requests_total{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}",protocol="http"}[5m])))))) * on (cluster_name,service) group_left(namespace,backend) ((max by (cluster_name,namespace,service,backend) (label_replace(sre_ingress_backend_info{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}",ingress_namespace!="",ingress_namespace=~"${ingress_namespace}",backend=~"${ingress_service}"}, "namespace", "$1", "ingress_namespace", "(.*)"))) or ((max by (cluster_name,namespace,service,backend) (label_replace(label_join(label_replace(kubernetes_state_ingress_path{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}",namespace=~"${ingress_namespace}",service=~"${ingress_service}"}, "backend", "$1", "service", "(.*)"), "service_key", "-", "namespace", "service", "kube_service_port"), "service", "$1@kubernetes", "service_key", "(.*)"))) unless on (cluster_name) (sre_ingress_inventory_success{cluster_name=~"${ingress_cluster}"}))))), "sre_series", "", "code")), "sre_series", "HTTP $1", "sre_series", "(.*)"))

display.description: Are requests reaching applications through Traefik, and where are errors or delays occurring?
display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **Are requests reaching applications through Traefik, and where are errors or delays occurring?** Traefik is the entry point that sends incoming requests to applications. Start with traffic, errors and response time, then select an application. Certificates and connections are cluster-wide measurements. **No data is not the same as zero.** Select a cluster before narrowing the next filters. **None** selects nothing; **Everything** selects all available values. After changing a cluster, reset the following filters to Everything. Full names and values opens the complete resource list.

display.description:
Average and percentile response times through Traefik. A higher 99% line reveals slow requests that the average may hide.

Measurement details:
Each point summarizes the preceding five minutes. Average adds all response times and divides by completed requests. Half of calls (p50) finished within that line's time; 95 of 100 (p95) and 99 of 100 (p99) show how long slower calls took. Example: p95 of 200 ms means about 95% finished within 200 ms and 5% took longer. Rising lines mean slower responses. Traefik estimates these percentiles from timing buckets; without calls, no response time can be calculated.
display.name: Response time over time (ms)

display.description:
About 95% of requests completed within this time over the last five minutes. Some requests can be slower; compare the 99% tile.

Measurement details:
If this shows 200 ms, about 95 out of 100 calls finished within 200 ms and the other five took longer. This is the p95 response time: it helps spot slow experiences that an average can hide. It is estimated from Traefik measurements for the selected applications over the last hour, including earlier tests. Lower means faster responses. Browser measurements can differ because they include extra network time. Uses the same five-minute window as average response time. The average can exceed p95 when a few requests take an exceptionally long time, such as long polling.

display.description:
Estimated traffic totals per application. A flat line is a summary for the selected period, not a trend.

Measurement details:
Uses the time period selected in the top toolbar. Sums non-overlapping counter changes at the chart resolution (minimum one minute) across the selected period. This is a metric estimate, not a per-request audit. Scrape gaps, new series and unavailable history can undercount activity. Totals are rounded for display. Scrape timing and partial interval boundaries affect the result. A longer selected period includes more history; it does not change the alert evaluation windows.
